itinerary.text: Midnight departure from Islamabad. Breakfast somewhere past Mardan, then the climb up the Swat valley. An hour at Bahrain bazaar, Blue Point in the afternoon, beds in Kalam by dark.
Out early for the jeep track — it is rough, and that is the point. Time at Mahodand lake, lunch, then the long drive back down. Islamabad the same night.

itinerary.text: Out of Islamabad in the dark and onto the Karakoram Highway. A full day of driving along the Indus to Chilas.
The Raikot jeep track — one of the more committing roads in the country — then the walk in to Fairy Meadows. Camp goes up, and the Holi colours come out in the evening.
The long day: up to Nanga Parbat Base Camp at 4,600 m and back down to the meadows before dark. Go slow, drink water.
Beyal camp in the morning, the rest of the day free at the meadows, then down to the jeeps and south along the Indus.

steps.p: Say which trip and how many seats. Wahid answers it himself, usually the same day.
A seat is yours once the advance is in — vans are small and August fills early.
Pickup points and the packing list go out there a few days before.
The driving happens while you sleep. You wake up in the mountains.

faqs.q: Where does the van leave from?
faqs.a: Islamabad, always, and usually around midnight so the driving happens while you sleep. Pickup points go out in the WhatsApp group a few days before. Drop-off is back at the same points.
The van both ways, your bed, the meals listed on the trip page, and the local jeeps where the road needs them. It does not cover what you buy on the way, gear hire, or meals we have not listed.

faqs.q: Do I have to be a student?
faqs.a: No. The dates are planned around semesters and the prices around student budgets, but the van is open to anyone who travels well in a group.

faqs.q: How do I hold a seat?
faqs.a: Message the number. A seat is yours once the advance is in — vans are small and August fills early.

faqs.q: Can I come on my own, or bring family?
faqs.a: Both happen on most trips. Rooms are allocated separately for women travelling alone or in groups.

faqs.q: How high do we actually go, and does that matter?
faqs.a: Kalam tops out at 2,865 m, which nobody feels. Nanga Parbat Base Camp is 4,600 m, high enough that you walk slowly, drink more water than you think you need, and tell me if your head hurts.
A warm layer even in August, shoes you can walk a jeep track in, a power bank, your ID card, and any medicine you take. A full list goes out in the group before we leave.

reviews.text: Everything was sorted before we reached the pickup point. First time north and I never once felt lost.
The price on the poster was the price we paid. That alone is rare here.
Small van, good food, and someone who knew exactly when to leave to beat the traffic.
